summary.signal: 航空エンジン開発では燃費目標だけでなく、耐久性、粉塵環境、熱・電力・推進統合、製造データまで含む設計・検証ループが前面に出ている。
Engineering/Scientific AIでは、Neural Operatorの領域移行、材料探索のhuman-in-the-loop、異種材料接合など、物理制約と検証可能性を残した実装が強い。
AI Agentの本番実装は、harnessやMCPそのものよりsandbox選択、identity attribution、tool-call inspection、実行前policy enforcementへ重心が移っている。
企業AIの効果測定では、導入率よりも雇用・業務変化を縦断的に追う分析と、因果と相関を分ける設計が重要になっている。

central_signals: 航空・重工系のデジタル化は、単独のAIモデルより試験、製造、物理モデル、システム統合まで含む閉ループへ進んでいる。
Scientific AIの有望な方向は、物理・数値計算を捨てることではなく、少量データ適応、人間介入、明示的制約を組み込むことにある。
Agentの企業導入では、実行環境と権限境界がモデル性能と同等以上に重要なシステム設計要素になっている。

OpenAI/F5のAgent基盤・セキュリティ機能は製品仕様であり、実運用での有効性は別途評価が必要。

selected.title: CFM RISE Open Fan: efficiency target is paired with durability and dust-ingestion validation
factual_points: CFM states that the RISE Open Fan architecture targets about 20% better fuel efficiency than conventional turbofan architectures.
The program explicitly treats durability in hot and harsh environments, including dust ingestion and erosion, as a design and test concern rather than a post-design issue.
CFM reports more than 350 tests and 3,000 core endurance cycles in the RISE technology program and describes dust-ingestion testing as part of the maturation path.
The test progression spans components, modules and system-level work, with flight demonstration planned later in the decade.

claims.text: CFM targets about 20% better fuel efficiency for the RISE Open Fan architecture.
CFM reports more than 350 tests and 3,000 core endurance cycles in the RISE maturation program.
CFM describes reduced dust ingestion and durability in harsh environments as intended benefits of the architecture and test program.

selected.why_it_matters: Next-generation engine optimization is being framed around a coupled objective set: fuel burn, operability, durability, environmental exposure and airframe integration. That is more representative of real propulsion design than a single efficiency metric.
selected.practical_implication: Track RISE claims as targets until test evidence matures, and treat dust/erosion durability and environment-specific validation as explicit design variables alongside aerodynamic efficiency.

selected.title: LatentDDM adapts neural operators to larger domains through learnable composition
factual_points: LatentDDM pretrains an operator on smaller subdomains and adapts to larger target domains by training a lightweight composition module rather than retraining the full operator.
The authors report 36–56% lower error on larger Darcy-flow domains after adaptation with only 16 target simulations.
The paper also reports improved multi-step field prediction in 20-step pitching-airfoil rollouts.

claims.text: The method separates local operator pretraining from a lightweight learnable composition module for target-domain adaptation.
The authors report 36–56% lower error after adaptation with 16 target simulations on larger Darcy domains.
The authors report improved 20-step pitching-airfoil rollouts after composition adaptation.

selected.why_it_matters: Engineering surrogates often fail when geometry or domain size changes. A decomposition that reuses a locally trained operator and adapts only the composition layer directly targets the cost of moving surrogate models between design domains.
selected.practical_implication: For CFD/CAE surrogate programs, evaluate transfer cost and target-simulation count alongside raw in-domain error; small adaptation modules may be more operationally useful than full-model retraining.

selected.title: SARA-H adds probabilistic phase identification and human guidance to autonomous materials exploration
factual_points: The SARA platform integrates probabilistic phase identification into an autonomous materials-exploration loop so synthesis choices can target phase regions rather than only scalar property values.
SARA-H adds human guidance to the reasoning loop and the authors report improved sampling efficiency in benchmarked search tasks.
The work includes robotic thin-film oxide exploration and active-learning experiments rather than remaining a simulation-only demonstration.

claims.text: SARA uses probabilistic phase identification to guide autonomous exploration toward target phase regions.
SARA-H incorporates human guidance into the autonomous reasoning loop and the authors report improved search efficiency.
The study includes robotic active-learning campaigns for thin-film oxide materials.

selected.why_it_matters: This is a concrete pattern for combining autonomous experimentation with expert intervention without reducing the human role to an emergency stop. Phase identification also makes the scientific state of the loop more interpretable than a black-box objective alone.
selected.practical_implication: Closed-loop materials R&D should expose structured scientific state, uncertainty and intervention points so domain experts can redirect search without discarding the automation stack.

selected.title: Pratt & Whitney AutoAir links factory location data, scanning and AI to fan-blade production
factual_points: RTX says fan-blade output at Pratt & Whitney AutoAir increased about 20% each year since 2024 while production time fell by roughly 20%.
The site uses real-time location data to replace manual tracking of more than 1,000 parts per shift and daily location checks.
Blue-light scanning creates 3D fan-blade data, and RTX describes an AI program being introduced to learn from prior scans and improve inspection accuracy.

claims.text: RTX reports approximately 20% annual fan-blade output growth since 2024 and roughly 20% lower production time at AutoAir.
The factory uses real-time location data to track more than 1,000 parts per shift and reduce manual searches.
RTX describes AI-assisted learning from historical blue-light scan data as part of the inspection workflow.

selected.why_it_matters: The useful industrial-AI pattern is the coupling of traceability, metrology and production data, not a standalone model. It is directly relevant to aero-engine manufacturing where part history and inspection state are already structured process assets.
selected.practical_implication: Manufacturing AI projects should first instrument part identity, routing and inspection data so AI can act on a reliable digital thread; treat reported throughput gains as site-specific until independently reproduced.

selected.title: GKN Aerospace receives Swedish future-combat-air contract covering thermal, electrical and propulsion technologies
selected.category: 航空機・主要サプライヤー
factual_points: Sweden's FMV awarded GKN Aerospace an approximately SEK 390 million contract under the Future Combat Air System Concept Programme.
The work runs through 2028 and includes concept studies, technology development and demonstrators.
GKN identifies thermal management, onboard electrical power and propulsion-related systems as strategic technology areas.

claims.text: The FMV contract is approximately SEK 390 million and runs through 2028.
The program covers concept studies, technology development and demonstrators in thermal management, onboard electrical power and propulsion-related systems.

selected.why_it_matters: Future combat-air propulsion is increasingly a vehicle-level thermal and electrical integration problem rather than an isolated engine-core problem. The contract scope makes that coupling explicit.
selected.practical_implication: For propulsion R&D, thermal management and onboard power should be treated as first-class architecture variables in MBSE and technology-demonstrator planning, not downstream interfaces.

selected.title: AVL and QinetiQ connect MBSE, digital twins, physics models and field validation for defence mobility
factual_points: AVL and QinetiQ announced a strategic partnership around model-based systems engineering and digital-twin methods for defence mobility programmes.
The described stack combines physics-based modelling, digital twins, virtual validation and physical field testing.
The companies frame a shared digital foundation as a way to mature designs earlier and reduce dependence on late physical testing.

claims.text: The partnership combines MBSE, physics-based modelling, digital twins, virtual validation and physical testing.
AVL and QinetiQ say the common digital foundation can raise design maturity earlier and reduce physical-test dependence.

selected.why_it_matters: The interesting signal is not defence mobility itself but the explicit virtual-to-field validation chain. This is the same integration problem faced by aerospace systems attempting to connect MBSE, CAE, test evidence and certification artifacts.
selected.practical_implication: Digital-engineering programs should define how model evidence survives the transition from virtual validation to physical test and how discrepancies feed back into the system model.

selected.title: OpenAI Agents API exposes harness, sandbox choice, MCP and subagent primitives as a managed agent runtime
selected.category: AIエージェント・開発基盤
factual_points: OpenAI launched the Agents API in public beta with an open-source Codex harness.
Developers can use OpenAI-managed sandboxes, their own infrastructure or partner execution environments.
The API includes MCP support, tool search/programmatic tool use, long-session context management and concurrent subagents.

claims.text: The Agents API is available in public beta and includes the open-source Codex harness.
The execution model supports OpenAI-hosted, customer-hosted and partner sandbox environments.
MCP, tool search, long-running context management and concurrent subagents are supported agent-runtime primitives.

selected.why_it_matters: Agent infrastructure is consolidating around a runtime contract that separates reasoning from execution environment, tool discovery and context lifecycle. That architecture is directly transferable to engineering-agent deployments.
selected.practical_implication: Engineering deployments should keep the harness portable across managed and self-hosted sandboxes, with explicit network, filesystem and credential policies outside the model itself.

selected.title: F5 Workforce AI Security moves agent controls into identity attribution and inline MCP tool inspection
factual_points: F5 announced a network-based control layer intended to attribute AI interactions to users or agents and retain identity/context around actions.
The product is described as inspecting MCP tool calls before execution and applying allow, block or modification policies.
F5 says general availability is planned for October 2026.

claims.text: F5 describes identity attribution and contextual policy for workforce AI and agent actions.
The announced control layer can inspect MCP tool calls and allow, block or modify them before execution.
F5 expects general availability in October 2026.

selected.why_it_matters: As agents gain tool access, security controls need to operate at the action boundary rather than only at prompt ingress. Identity-aware tool-call inspection is a concrete implementation of that requirement.
selected.practical_implication: For CAD/CAE/HPC agents, policy should bind user identity, agent identity, tool, arguments and execution context before the action reaches license servers, filesystems, schedulers or PLM systems.

selected.title: Gusto longitudinal study associates AI adoption with faster small-business hiring
factual_points: The analysis follows 1,593 AI-using firms and 669 AI-aware non-adopters identified from Gusto's 2025 survey and links them to subsequent payroll records.
Using an event-study design, Gusto reports roughly 7% higher headcount in the first year after adoption relative to the comparison group.
For firms with fewer than 10 employees, the reported differential is about 10%, with larger effects in some community-service businesses.
The study is observational and does not establish that AI adoption caused the hiring difference.

claims.text: The longitudinal sample contains 1,593 AI adopters and 669 AI-aware non-adopters linked to Gusto payroll data.
Gusto reports about 7% higher first-year headcount growth after AI adoption, with about 10% for firms below 10 employees.
The research design is observational and supports association rather than causal proof.

selected.why_it_matters: The report is more useful than a one-time adoption survey because it links stated AI adoption to subsequent payroll behavior. It also challenges the simplistic assumption that AI uptake necessarily maps to immediate headcount reduction.
selected.practical_implication: Enterprise AI measurement should pair adoption telemetry with longitudinal operational outcomes such as headcount, throughput and task mix, while preserving a clear distinction between association and causality.

report_details.methodology: Longitudinal observational study linking an April 2025 survey to quarterly Gusto payroll records; 1,593 AI adopters and 669 AI-aware non-adopters; event-study approach using the Callaway-Sant'Anna framework and pre-trend checks.
key_metrics: approximately 7% higher headcount in the first year after adoption
approximately 10% higher headcount for firms with fewer than 10 employees
approximately 19% differential reported for small community-service firms
report_details.comparison_to_previous: Not a repeated annual wave; the study compares post-adoption trajectories with a contemporaneous non-adopter group using longitudinal payroll data.
report_details.practical_meaning: AI adoption among these small businesses is associated with expansion rather than a simple substitution of labor, but the design cannot establish causal effects.
report_details.caveats: Observational rather than randomized; AI adoption timing is survey-based; Gusto customers are not a random sample of all firms; sector and growth-selection effects may remain despite robustness checks.

selected.title: NIMS develops printable porous anchor for strong joining of dissimilar hard and soft materials
factual_points: NIMS developed a porous anchoring layer that can be formed by coating a solution and drying it through viscoelastic phase separation.
The joint combines chemical affinity at one interface with mechanical interlocking at the porous interface, enabling hard/soft dissimilar-material bonding.
NIMS reports bond strength above 7 MPa and roughly double the vertical tensile strength of a comparison configuration.
The work was published in Small on 2026-09-10.

claims.text: The porous anchor is formed through a coat-and-dry process based on viscoelastic phase separation.
NIMS reports bond strength exceeding 7 MPa and approximately twofold vertical tensile improvement in the reported tests.
The corresponding Small article was published on 2026-09-10.

selected.why_it_matters: Multi-material joining is a recurring bottleneck in lightweight structures, sensors and compliant systems. The method is notable because it achieves anchoring through a printable porous layer rather than a geometry-specific macroscopic fastener.
selected.practical_implication: Evaluate the method for interface durability, temperature/environmental stability and manufacturability on application-specific material pairs before extrapolating the reported static bond strength.

selected.title: K2 Horizon releases a six-model open stack with intermediate checkpoints and training artifacts
factual_points: K2 Horizon is released as a six-model family spanning approximately 0.9B to 375B total parameters.
The release includes final weights plus intermediate checkpoints, training code, logs, evaluation artifacts and either datasets or detailed data-construction recipes.
Models and code are released under Apache 2.0, with day-zero support described for common local/serving runtimes including vLLM, SGLang and Ollama.

claims.text: K2 Horizon provides six model sizes from roughly 0.9B to 375B parameters with Apache-2.0 model/code licensing.
The release includes intermediate checkpoints, training code, logs, evaluations and data or reproducible data-construction recipes.

selected.why_it_matters: For research and enterprise evaluation, access to intermediate checkpoints and training artifacts is materially more useful than weights alone. It supports reproducibility, adaptation research and failure analysis.
selected.practical_implication: When comparing open models, score artifact completeness, licensing and reproducibility separately from benchmark performance; avoid treating self-reported frontier-performance claims as independent evidence.

wildcards.title: Adaptive rocket trajectory optimization combines reinforcement learning with FPGA inference
factual_points: The peer-reviewed study combines deep reinforcement learning and FPGA-based inference for reusable-rocket trajectory optimization.
The design targets adaptive onboard optimization rather than offline-only trajectory planning.

claims.text: The study combines reinforcement learning with FPGA execution for adaptive reusable-rocket trajectory optimization.
claims.evidence_location: Scout-captured journal metadata; primary page could not be reopened during limited Curator verification

wildcards.why_it_matters: Hardware-constrained onboard inference is a useful counterpoint to cloud-scale agent work and could matter for flight systems where latency, power and deterministic execution dominate.
wildcards.practical_implication: Track whether the method is evaluated under realistic guidance uncertainty, hardware timing and safety constraints before inferring flight-readiness.

wildcards.title: Cohere fuses decode stages into a megakernel for North Mini Code serving
factual_points: Cohere describes a decode megakernel that fuses execution stages conventionally launched as separate GPU kernels.
On a single H100 in BF16, Cohere reports approximately 1.25–1.41x end-to-end decode-throughput improvement versus vLLM in its tested configurations.
The implementation is accompanied by code and accuracy comparisons, but the throughput figures remain vendor-run benchmarks.

claims.text: The serving design fuses multiple decode stages into a megakernel rather than launching them as separate kernels.
Cohere reports 1.25–1.41x end-to-end decode-throughput gains versus vLLM on a single H100 BF16 benchmark setup.

wildcards.why_it_matters: Agent workloads amplify decode and orchestration overhead because they perform many iterative calls. Kernel-level serving efficiency can therefore affect system economics even when model quality is unchanged.
wildcards.practical_implication: Compare throughput under the intended batch size, context length and hardware rather than transferring a single-H100 vendor benchmark directly to production economics.

wildcards.title: TimesFM-3 extends zero-shot foundation forecasting to native multivariate prediction
factual_points: Google Research describes TimesFM-3 as a 330M-parameter time-series foundation model with native multivariate zero-shot forecasting in a single forward pass.
Google states that pretraining used more than one trillion time points and cites manufacturing, observability and natural-science use cases.

claims.text: TimesFM-3 is a 330M-parameter model designed for native multivariate zero-shot forecasting.
Google reports pretraining on more than one trillion time points and identifies manufacturing among target domains.

wildcards.why_it_matters: Multivariate zero-shot forecasting could reduce bespoke model development for condition monitoring and operations data, but industrial value depends on calibration, drift and failure-mode behavior rather than benchmark averages alone.
wildcards.practical_implication: If evaluated for manufacturing, test across regime shifts, missing sensors and rare-event periods before replacing domain-specific forecasting pipelines.
